title: Arrival at Emon
summary: Ayante and his master Diomedes arrive in Tal'Dorei by skyship, taking in Emon — the city of wide stairs and mahogany roofs.

title: The Meeting at Gilmore's
summary: In Emon's academic district, Ayante finds Gilmore's shop wreathed in magical fireworks. Overhearing Sorfon ask after an ancient temple, his mockery turns to respect once he learns Sorfon serves Pelor.

title: A Pact Beneath the Sun
summary: Bare arms clasped beneath the noon sun, Ayante and Sorfon seal their pact. Diomedes departs for Stilben, and the two devotees of Pelor set out together.

title: Screams from Greyskull Keep
summary: Sorfon and Ayante meet in a small plaza near the locked Keep as screams erupt from inside. Ereldra lingers behind. Mortis is already within, following the Raven Queen's golden thread.

title: The Book of Baba Yaga
summary: Slipping away from the others, Mortis finds a heavy tome pinned to a hallway shelf by an axe. He pries it open and discovers it belongs to Baba Yaga — grandmother of all witches. It snaps shut before he finishes, and he cannot reopen it.

title: Sarenrae's Anger
summary: Sorfon prays in the Keep's chapel and contacts Sarenrae directly. The goddess is angered by his lifelong devotion to Pelor alone, but gives a cryptic clue: 'The temple is just a temple; follow YOUR light.'

title: Allura Vysoren Intervenes
summary: The archmage Allura Vysoren arrives to investigate the disturbance. She freezes Mortis, revealing him as the apparent ghost, then casts a bind spell linking him to Sorfon's armor. The party is named Mortis's wardens and charged with a future mission to repair the damages caused.

title: Long Rest at the Keep
summary: The party settles in for a long rest at Greyskull Keep. Allura confirms that Pike Trickfoot is in Issylra. Two hours remain before Mortis's bind spell expires.

title: The Vigil for Cassandra
summary: The dragon driven off, Cassandra de Rolo lies fallen in the ruined palace. Mortis reaches for her departing spirit before it slips beyond reach.

title: Returning the Barûk-Kazad
summary: The party restores the legendary dwarven axe to Kraghammer and escorts Cassandra's body from the palace. Both bounties are claimed — 4,800 gp — and Sorfon is named Emissary of Kraghammer.

title: Percy's Word
summary: Through the carriage's communicator, Percy confirms the soul has roughly ten days in limbo — and that a true resurrection is far harder than the party had hoped.

title: The Patron in the Hoard
summary: Over the Ozmit Sea, the ancient red dragon Ashardalon reaches Ereldra from atop a vast hoard — claiming her as patron and demanding to know why they strayed from Whitestone.

title: Pelor's Charge
summary: Pelor speaks to Sorfon: bear the sun-god's incense from the Temple of Pelor to the Temple of Sarenrae, protect the surviving de Rolos — and first put Ayante to the test.

title: The Gates of Vasselheim
summary: Magic items surrendered to the city guard, the party passes the walls — racing to revive Cassandra before her soul moves on.

igLabel: Day 38 · Chapel of Pelor, High Pass
title: The Censer of Pelor
summary: In Pelor's chapel the custodian finally hands over the sealed silver urn of incense. It must now be carried some 7 km across Vasselheim to the Temple of Sarenrae. Sorfon and Ayante swear to guard the chapel's sacred texts and take up pilgrim rights.

title: Caval's Grave
summary: Down in the crypt, Ereldra reads the inscription over a grave — 'Here lies Caval' — written in a shadar-kai dialect. Mortis tells her what he remembers of his betrayer, and the two agree to keep it between them.

title: The Fate of the Witch's Book
summary: Above ground the party finally argues out what to do with Baba Yaga's book — bound in human skin, clasped with teeth. Burning it would only return it to the witch, so it is stowed in the bag of holding; Mortis vows to warn the others before ever opening it.

title: The Imp at Ubu's Feet
summary: See Invisibility reveals an imp riding at the feet of Ubu, their oblivious Bahamut guard — a familiar spying on the party. Under threat it names its master: La Toma, the Slayer's Take, who hunt Mortis. The party kills it, though a familiar can always be re-summoned.

title: The Archon of Bahamut
summary: The white-robed man from the crossroads is revealed as the Archon of Bahamut — bald and tall in silver and pale blue, the most powerful man in the city this cycle. Bahamut's faith governs Vasselheim, and his eyes are now on the party.

title: The Raven Queen's Thread
summary: At a deep gnome trader's stall a golden thread — the Raven Queen's mark — singles out a single scroll: Speak with Dead, the spell Mortis has hunted since Kraghammer. The session ends mid-purchase, a dead imp still at their feet.

title: The Deck of Illusions
summary: The party finishes its business at the deep gnome's stall and draws from a Deck of Illusions — reusable cards of pure illusion, not the deadly Deck of Many Things. With the shopping done they take Cassandra up toward the High Pass.

title: The Bounty on Locus
summary: La Toma seizes a white-haired dampir out of the crowd. Rather than let him be killed, Sorfon pays the 200 gp bounty to Hungar (?), the bear-cloaked orc hunter, and claims Locus for himself — meaning to redeem him. The contract only truly lifts once La Toma's leader, Ocisa (?), is dealt with.

igLabel: Day 38 · Chapel of Pelor, High Pass
title: Cassandra Laid in Pelor's Chapel
summary: Marco, the lone custodian, grants the party the pilgrim rites and Cassandra's body is laid out on the third floor. Holy water splashed on Ereldra burns her. Sorfon swears again to guard Pelor's sacred texts while they lodge in the chapel.

title: What the Witch's Book Says of Locus
summary: Baba Yaga's book gives up Locus's history: he is the last living subject of a Strahd and Baba Yaga project to breed vampire monster-hunters, and he is bound by a Geas — compelled, and hurt if he acts against it, as when he tries to speak of the book.

igLabel: Day 39 · The palace shrine of all gods
title: The Shadar-kai's Answer
summary: In the small hours Mortis prays to the Raven Queen at the shrine of all gods. Her hooded shadar-kai answer: Pike Trickfoot is beneath the Temple of Sarenrae, and can drive the diamond through Cassandra's chest as a catalyst to call her soul back. About six days of limbo remain.

title: Bahamut at the Palace Gate
summary: At about four in the morning the white-robed Archon reveals himself as Bahamut, the Platinum Dragon. Haftifaflmorhen is no monster but a victim — maddened by Torog (?) and made to devour his best friend. Bahamut refuses to take the Barûk-Kazad — left under guard in Kraghammer, yet only a summons away through Ereldra's pact — and counsels the party to keep its location secret; Ereldra covers her cursed eye at his request.

igLabel: Day 39 · The inn, the small hours
title: Locus Comes Down from the Ceiling
summary: Mortis finds Locus clinging to the ceiling mid-feed and coaxes him down. The dampir keeps to animals and shuns people, feeding only every few weeks — the surest sign that something human is left in him to redeem.

igLabel: Day 39 · The inn, the small hours
title: The Everlight's Charge
summary: Sorfon wakes with his Everlight talisman burning against his chest. A holy-water purification carries him to Sarenrae, who tells him every soul deserves redemption and asks him to get Locus out of the city and away from La Toma. She points him toward an old ally, and toward the links Ereldra keeps hidden.

title: Mortis Dies to Reach the Raven Queen
summary: Mortis dies by his own hand to cross into the Shadowfell and stand before his matron. The Raven Queen — his lover once, when she was mortal and he was Morgas — tells him Ravenloft and Barovia were torn out of her realm by the vampire Strahd, that Locus was bred to be Strahd's hound, and that her champion Vax'ildan can one day guide the party across. Then she sends him back.

title: Pelor Names Torog
summary: Pelor rebukes Sorfon for saving an undead, then answers him: the last and most dangerous Betrayer God he cast down was Torog, the Crawling King, pierced with lances of sunlight and sealed in the Far Realm. From that prison Torog corrupted Haftifaflmorhen. Saving the dragon or killing him ends the same — his mind is gone, so grant him rest.

title: The Council on the Axe
summary: With both gods' answers in hand the party decides: keep the Barûk-Kazad, hand it to no dragon, and set a trap for Haftifaflmorhen once they are strong enough to put him down. Ereldra admits outright that her patron Ashardalon's plan is genocide, and Mortis recalls an old nightmare in which Torog offered to free him and take Ashardalon's place at her shoulder.

title: The Forge of Tyr
summary: The commissions are ready. Tyr gives Ayante the Helm of the Wrathbringer (?) for free — it makes foes fear him, so long as his head stays on his shoulders — and hands Sorfon plate reforged from his old chainmail, stamped with the Dwendalian owl-eyes. A one-eyed soldier's spirit, Aldis (?), is caught in the metal and can be summoned as an ally each fight; the armor once belonged to Gerard Cousland (?), likely Sorfon's kin.

igLabel: Day 40 · Chapel of Pelor, High Pass
title: Cassandra Carried Out
summary: Pelor's custodian gives Cassandra the last sacraments, in case the resurrection fails, and the party lifts her body to carry it to Pike. Locus cannot set foot in Pelor's temple and waits outside. The route is set — the post office, then supplies, then the Temple of Sarenrae — with about six days of limbo left.

title: Letters from the Palace Tower
summary: Ubu, on guard and strictly business, leads the party up a palace tower to the messenger loft, where a tiny, wrinkled gnome seals the post and a flamingo, a pelican and the pigeons carry it off. Ereldra pays double to reach her family, far away. A second letter tells the Council of Kraghammer that the party will call the Barûk-Kazad to them as bait to draw Haftifaflmorhen away — its sender answering for the axe and promising its return.

title: Pike in the Garden
summary: At the Temple of Sarenrae — a wooden hall with a bell tower, marble obelisks and an unlit pyre beneath a hanging idol — the high priestess, Tessa (?), whose ruby-like skin shifts through reds and oranges, sends Sorfon back outside: the small, scarred gardener he passed is Pike Trickfoot. Rushing back, he collides with her and sprawls in his plate. He hands her the sealed urn of Pelor's incense — meant, since she is only visiting, for the temple itself — and learns that Grog is in Westruun, living the adventurer's life.

title: The Burr Pendant
summary: Resting on the temple steps, Ereldra weighs entrusting her two siblings to Fungrim (?), and Mortis glimpses the pendant he gave her: a spiked burr that recalls the half-mad dwarf who climbed Haftifaflmorhen at Kraghammer, laughing as he fought. It breathes pestilence and overflowing madness, seems worked by the same hands as Ereldra's pact, with a different finish, and opens to call him. Ashardalon knows of her siblings, if not where they are; Mortis talks her out of it.

title: Cassandra Breathes Again
summary: Mortis's Gentle Repose has bought enough time. Pike calls the high priestess for a bed, and as light pours from her hands the diamond sinks into Cassandra's chest: Cassandra draws breath. Pale, exhausted and racked by migraines, she remembers nothing of the dragon. She takes Pike's hand and thanks the party — it is beyond price.

title: Percy Drops from the Sky
summary: Through the carriage's pearl, Pike tells Percy his sister is well. After a long silence the ground shakes and his droning flying machine drifts in over the city, slow as a zeppelin; Percy drops from it, lands with style and weeps at Cassandra's bedside. He offers the party passage anywhere, and agrees to a short stop at Sarenrae's ancient temple — Pike marks it on their map of Issylra, some 27 km north in the mountains — before his last stop: Whitestone.

title: Barovia on No Map
summary: Mortis asks how Cassandra became a dampir, as he had understood from his goddess; Percy corrects him — the vampire Sylas Briarwood only enthralled her, and he is dead. Introduced to Locus, Percy has never heard of Strahd or Barovia, and none of the party's maps shows it. Mortis remembers Ravenloft as one of the few floating cities of the Age of Arcanum, spared the Calamity when the von Zarovich family, who had stolen it, drew it into the Shadowfell — it may have drifted anywhere since.

title: The Siege of Dis
summary: As Pike starts to name someone who lived through the Calamity, Ereldra's eye catches fire and her soul, trailing a silver thread, is torn away to the Nine Hells. Amid a slaughter of demons and devils, Ashardalon breathes green fire on the metal fortress of Dis, while infernal machines, loaded by imps with flasks of a pale green liquid, loose skull-shaped bolts that blow it apart. In Vasselheim her body bleeds from a wound no blade made; Sorfon's Hunter's Mark finds her soul leagues beneath the ground.

title: Ashardalon's Demand
summary: Blinking across the battlefield, Ereldra lands at her patron's side under seventeen blades. Ashardalon takes an elven form — horns draconic and infernal, dark sclera, yellow eyes. He means to take the rest of the Hells by brute force, but his shots are numbered and his residuum is rubbish: he wants the white stone beneath Whitestone, refined. An imp brings a black parchment — kill a lamb, pour its blood on it and throw all the residuum upon it. Of his fourteen warlocks she works best; then he crushes the imp spying on her and sends her back.

title: Percy's Black Powder
summary: Back in her body, Ereldra describes the machines, and Percy recognises his own work: black powder — his design, an invention of pure hatred meant to kill five people, which Ripley mass-produced at the cost of her life — now taken further than humans, elves or dwarves could. The machines need refined residuum, so what Ereldra delivers could wreck them if blended with something oily and combustible. She must be the first of the fourteen to deliver; Percy wants them in his laboratory in Whitestone.

title: The Imp's Lie
summary: Warned that someone is spying, the party hunts for the watcher. Mortis now believes the imp at Ubu's feet lied about La Toma to shield its master. Divine Sense and See Invisibility reveal another imp at their feet; Sorfon seizes it, Mortis charms it with Friends, and it names Fungrim (?) as its master, seven blocks away with La Toma. Ereldra smashes the burr pendant — a reek of cod and rotting entrails, a lure — and Fungrim comes running.

title: Beams from the Mountain
summary: Fungrim arrives shouting for everyone to get down — and a beam from the mountain slams into Mortis. Ayante covers him with his shield, and another shot finds them as they fall back into the temple. The shooter is Elías, in a cave some 3 km northwest. Behind barred doors Fungrim warns Ereldra that Ashardalon has told his other warlocks she must die, and that he refused. The imp was Elías's familiar all along, lying for its master while it found him a clean shot at her.

title: Eggs, Disguises and a Back Door
summary: Behind barred doors the party plans its way to a sniper some 8 km up the slope. Percy brings three mechanical eggs — smoke charges that work like Pass Without Trace. Elías won't shoot Fungrim, so Fungrim will stage a fight, Mortis will take Ereldra's shape to play her, and Ayante — stripped to his shorts and sword — will run for the heights. The high priestess, her skin now like cooling magma, shows them a hidden way out through the temple garden to the mountain.

title: The Staged Fight
summary: Fungrim kicks Sorfon out through the door and beats him for real — 'if I don't, he won't believe a thing: he knows me' — his corroding glow and poison leaving Sorfon badly hurt, while Mortis, wearing Ereldra's face, plays the wounded victim. Elías's shots rain down: Mortis's Shield turns one, another strikes Fungrim himself. Meanwhile Ayante, unseen, races up the mountain.

title: Ayante's Mushroom
summary: Halfway up, camouflaged in mud, Ayante forages a wild mushroom for strength and eats it. The hillside tilts, the sun stops and the stars stretch; he sweats through a dazzling trip, nearly passes out and plunges his face into a stream — the visions fade, but the drug and an aching exhaustion stay with him.

title: Elías by the Stream
summary: By a stream a man in boots and a hat — Elías — finds the drugged Ayante and, pistol levelled, tosses him leaves that clear his head. Once Ayante washes the mud off, Elías knows him: from a bar in Emon where Ayante killed several dwarves — his noisy band is hard to forget. Ayante stalls, giving his companions' names backwards and begging a last rite sacred to Ilión; Elías, disgusted, collars him with an imp's invisible chain and backs away, gun still trained on him.

title: A Stone, a Fist and a Pistol
summary: Chained, Ayante hurls a stone that knocks the pistol from Elías's hand, then surges in and floors him with his fists — but the pistol flies back to its owner's grip. Neither will back down. Ayante spits at his eye and dives behind a tree; Elías 'doesn't need both eyes' to see him there. In the chase they collide and tumble, and Elías's shots tear into Ayante before he breaks away, bleeding.

title: Agro (?) and the Climb
summary: A wild shot into the sky tells the party something has gone wrong, and they head up. They find Elías's jet-black horse, Agro (?), which remembers Ereldra from a camp they once shared with Elías and Fungrim — the night it kicked a cauldron onto Fungrim after his prank on her. Sorfon and Mortis ride the long way and get up a 24 m wall by magic; Ereldra takes a shortcut, Fungrim stuck to her back by his burr armour, and Misty Steps them both over the last cliff.

title: Locus Tastes Blood
summary: Fungrim conjures a snout of purple flies and follows Elías's smell of leather oil; the tracks tell of a collision and smoking bullet-holes in the earth. At a drop of blood Locus breaks: he tastes it, veins rise across his face and his sclera darkens. Overstimulated, he can now follow two bloods — two wounded people — and Sorfon walks at his back, ready to knock him out.

igLabel: Day 40 · The clearing on the mountain
title: The Clearing
summary: In a ring-shaped clearing under the drizzle they find Ayante slumped on a rock, bleeding out; one of Percy's smoke eggs covers Sorfon's dash to heal him. As they carry him out, the invisible imp at his neck pulls a cord and its bomb bursts on Ayante and Sorfon; then shots strike Sorfon from the north. Sorfon calls up Aldis, who splits into two spirits — one with a shield — that bring Elías down in the bushes; Aldis takes a last shot for Sorfon and fades, burning. Elías rises, pistol in hand, facing them all.
